text: Some have theorized that performing eccentric actions at higher velocities enhances anabolism as a result of increased tension on muscle during high-speed lengthening. Roschel and colleagues (198) found similar activation of Akt, mTOR, and p70 S6K following 5 sets of 8 eccentric repetitions at a slow (20° per second) versus fast (210° per second) velocity, suggesting that the velocity of eccentric actions does not influence intracellular anabolic signaling. Several studies have shown a benefit from faster eccentric actions.
